Jorge Assis, PhD // Nord University, Norway // biodiversityDS, Centre of Marine Sciences, Portugal

Species occurrence data

Plotting species occurrence data

biodiversityDS .

Species distribution models require georeferenced records of occurrence (e.g. species locations, which is the response or dependent variable). Such data are widely available in digital format (e.g., online repositories like GBIF).

The first approach to the data is to map the occurrence records to depict the species distribution. This is done by plotting the occurrence records on a map of the study area.

# load libraries
library(terra)
# read occurrence records
records <- read.table("../Data/Text delimited/species_presence_records.csv", sep = ";", header = TRUE)
# transform data.frame into a spatial object
records <- vect(records, geom = c("Lon", "Lat"))
# read a landmass polygon
landmass <- vect("../Data/Vector data/Landmass/landmass.shp")
# crop landmass to the european Extent
mediterraneanExtent <- ext(-35, 45, 25, 55)
landmassMediterranean <- crop(landmass, mediterraneanExtent)
S3 // Downloading and managing biodiversity data in R

biodiversityDS .
# plot the landmass and the records
plot(landmassMediterranean, main = "Species occurrence records", col = "Gray", border = "Gray",
    axes = TRUE)
plot(records, col = "Black", pch = 19, cex = 0.5, add = TRUE)

Combining multiple data sources

biodiversityDS .

To combine records of occurrence based on data.frames, the rbind() function can be used. This function combines two or more data.frames by rows, creating a new data.frame that contains all the rows from each of the original data.frames. The number of columns and their names must be the same.

records <- rbind(recordsGbif, recordsObis)
# plot the records
plot(records[, c("Lon", "Lat")], col = "Black", pch = 19, cex = 0.5)

S3 // Biodiversity data in R

Data cleaning in R

biodiversityDS .

Remove NA coordinates

In species distribution modelling it is important to remove records with missing coordinates. This is because these records do not provide any information about the species distribution.

# inspect the number of records with NA coordinates
sum(is.na(records$Lon) | is.na(records$Lat))
## [1] 238
# remove NA coordinates
records <- records[!is.na(records$Lon) & !is.na(records$Lat), ]
# inspect the number of records
nrow(records)
## [1] 3563
S3 // Biodiversity data in R

biodiversityDS .

Remove duplicate coordinates

In species distribution models, duplicate coordinates are not useful. A species recorded at the same location multiple times does not add any new information to the model, and redundant information can introduce bias in the model. Therefore, it is important to remove duplicate coordinates from the dataset.

# inspect the number of duplicated records
sum(duplicated(records))
## [1] 1720
# remove duplicate coordinates
records <- records[!duplicated(records), ]
# inspect the number of records
nrow(records)
## [1] 1843
S3 // Biodiversity data in R

biodiversityDS .
# transform data.frame into a spatial object
records <- vect(records, geom = c("Lon", "Lat"))
# plot the landmass and the records
plot(landmass, main = "Species occurrence records", col = "Gray", border = "Gray", axes = TRUE)
plot(records, col = "Black", pch = 19, cex = 0.5, add = TRUE)

S3 // Downloading and managing biodiversity data in R

biodiversityDS .

Remove records outside the known geographic distributions

In species distribution models, it is important to remove the records that are outside the known distribution of species. Import or generate (i.e., to draw) vector data - a polygon - depicting the global distribution of the species of interest.

# Load necessary libraries
library(leaflet)
library(mapedit)

# create a base leaflet map
baseMap <- leaflet()
baseMap <- addTiles(baseMap)

# drawing vector polygon in the Viewer pane
myRegion <- drawFeatures(baseMap)
S3 // Downloading and managing biodiversity data in R

biodiversityDS .
# inspect the generated polygon depicting the distribution of the species
plot(landmass, main = "Global landmass", col = "gray", border = "gray", axes = TRUE)
plot(myRegion, border = "black", col = "black", add = TRUE)
plot(records, col = "red", pch = 19, cex = 0.5, add = TRUE)

S3 // Downloading and managing biodiversity data in R

biodiversityDS .

Intersect the polygon with the occurrence records to exclude those outside the known distribution of the species.

# Load necessary libraries
library(terra)
# transform the sf object to a terra object
myRegion <- vect(myRegion)
# intersect the records with the region
records <- intersect(records, myRegion)
# inspect the class of the object
class(records)
## [1] "SpatVector"
## attr(,"package")
## [1] "terra"
S3 // Downloading and managing biodiversity data in R

biodiversityDS .
# plot the distribution of the species without records outside the known distribution
plot(landmass, main = "Global landmass", col = "gray", border = "gray", axes = TRUE)
plot(records, color = "black", pch = 16, cex = 0.5, add = TRUE)

Remove records outside the known vertical distributions

Import a bathymetry layer and remove records outside the known vertical distribution of the species.

# import bathymetry layer
bathymetry <- rast("../Data/Raster data/Bathymetry.tif")
# plot the bathymetry layer and the records of occurrence
plot(bathymetry, main = "Bathymetry", axes = TRUE)
plot(records, color = "black", pch = 16, cex = 0.5, add = TRUE)

S3 // Downloading and managing biodiversity data in R

biodiversityDS .
# extract the values of the bathymetry based on the records
depthDistribution <- extract(bathymetry, records)
# plot the distribution of the depth records
hist(depthDistribution$Bathymetry, breaks = 500)

S3 // Downloading and managing biodiversity data in R

biodiversityDS .
# extract the depth values of the records
records <- records[depthDistribution$Bathymetry > -30 & !is.na(depthDistribution$Bathymetry),
    ]
# extract the depth values of the records
depthDistribution <- extract(bathymetry, records)
# plot the distribution of the depth records
hist(depthDistribution$Bathymetry, breaks = 500)

Final spatial dataset of records of occurrence of the species of interest without NA coordinates, duplicate coordinates, and records outside the known geographic and vertical distribution.

# plot the final records
plot(landmass, main = "Final dataset of occurrence records", col = "gray", border = "gray", axes = TRUE)
plot(records, color = "black", pch = 16, cex = 0.5, add = TRUE)
